question: What is another common name for healthcare-associated infections?
explanation: Nosocomial is the traditional medical term for infections that originate in a hospital environment. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: When does an infection officially count as a healthcare-associated infection?

options.A: Before the patient ever enters the clinic
options.C: At least 48 hours after hospital admission
options.D: Within the first two hours of arrival

explanation: The 48-hour window helps differentiate infections the patient brought in with them from those caught while inside the facility. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: How many total links make up the standard chain of infection?
explanation: The chain consists of six interdependent links, and breaking any single one stops the spread. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does a susceptible host represent in the chain of infection?

options.A: A medical instrument sterilized prior to a procedure
options.B: A person who lacks resistance to a specific pathogen
options.C: The physical surface where bacteria live and multiply
options.D: The specific pathway a virus uses to leave the body

explanation: A susceptible host is an individual whose immune system is weak or compromised enough to allow an infection to take hold. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: Who should standard precautions be applied to in a healthcare setting?
explanation: Standard precautions are universal and apply to every patient, because infection status is not always known. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary underlying assumption of standard precautions?

options.A: Gloves replace the need for washing your hands
options.B: Only visible blood contains dangerous bacterial pathogens
options.C: All body fluids can potentially transmit infectious agents
options.D: Healthy patients require no protective measures at all

explanation: Treating all body fluids as potentially infectious prevents accidental exposure to hidden pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative-pressure room?
explanation: Airborne precautions require special negative-pressure ventilation to keep infectious particles from escaping into the hallway. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which specific protective gear must the nurse wear before entering the room?
explanation: Tuberculosis is airborne, meaning staff must wear a fitted N95 respirator to filter out tiny suspended droplet nuclei. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the minimum recommended time for washing hands with soap and water?
explanation: Washing for at least 20 seconds gives friction and soap enough time to mechanically remove and destroy transient microorganisms. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why must a nurse use soap and water instead of alcohol gel after caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile?

options.A: Alcohol rubs do not reliably destroy bacterial spores
options.B: Soap and water dry out the skin much faster
options.C: Spores dissolve instantly when exposed to hand sanitizer
options.D: Alcohol gel leaves a sticky residue on surgical gloves

explanation: Clostridioides difficile produces tough spores that resist alcohol sanitizers, requiring physical washing to rinse them away. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: When taking off personal protective equipment, which item should you remove first?
explanation: Gloves are typically the most contaminated item, so removing them first prevents transferring pathogens to other pieces of PPE or your skin. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the correct sequence when putting on personal protective equipment before entering an isolation room?
explanation: Putting the gown on first and gloves last ensures the glove cuffs overlap the gown sleeves, leaving no exposed skin at the wrist. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: Where must a urinary catheter collection bag be positioned at all times to prevent backflow?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Resting on the floor of the room

explanation: Gravity keeps urine flowing downward away from the bladder, preventing contaminated urine from flowing back up into the tubing. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of using strict aseptic technique during invasive procedures?

options.A: To neutralize chemical toxins released by resident skin flora
options.B: To eliminate all pathogenic microorganisms from the sterile field
options.C: To reduce the total number of bacteria on non-porous furniture
options.D: To remove visible dirt and oil from the patient's outer skin

explanation: Aseptic technique aims to protect susceptible body sites by ensuring zero pathogens are introduced during invasive tasks. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Where should used injection needles be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: A red biohazard bag for soft waste
options.B: A standard black plastic trash bag
options.D: The side pocket of the nurse's uniform

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries for nurses and housekeeping staff. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Which practice should nurses avoid when handling used injection needles?

options.B: Dropping it straight into a bin
options.C: Carrying it in a dedicated tray

explanation: Recapping needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and should never be done. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to perform effective infection surveillance?

options.A: They perform all terminal room cleaning procedures
options.B: They spend the most direct time at the patient's bedside
options.C: They are solely responsible for writing hospital policy
options.D: They process laboratory blood cultures in the hospital lab

explanation: Continuous bedside interaction allows nurses to spot early warning signs of infection long before lab results return. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)
